hypothesis: For the calibrated paraxial eyes without an external lens, accommodation equals object demand while the required physical source diameter scales inversely with demand; therefore doubling demand from 60 D to 120 D halves source diameter and exceeds all supplied accommodation limits.
limitations: All requested 60–120 D cases are accommodation-infeasible under the supplied biological limits; source sizes remain conditional geometric solutions.
External-lens combinations at 90–120 D require a revised mechanical geometry because the requested object plane lies inside the provisional human lens vertex distance.
Absolute irradiance and biological safety remain out of scope without measured radiometry, exposure, spectrum, and tissue transmission.
The model remains a paraxial effective thin-eye model rather than a multi-surface anatomical eye.
next_step: Confirm the intended mechanical placement for ultra-near sources, then acquire measured radiometry and implement multi-surface anatomical eye and non-sequential stray-light models.
objective: Replace the finite object-demand sweep with 60–120 D in 10 D increments, regenerate all model outputs and reports, and preserve a physically valid external-lens reference.
observations: The requested demand grid is exactly 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 110, and 120 D.
Adult and child source diameters decrease from 5.988 mm at 60 D to 2.994 mm at 120 D; chick diameters decrease from 5.952 mm to 2.976 mm.
All 21 requested eye-demand combinations exceed the accommodation limits supplied in the source presentation.
The 90–120 D human object distances are shorter than the provisional 12 mm external-lens vertex distance, so those combinations are not modeled with an external lens.
A separate 10 D external-lens reference preserves the prior sensitivity analysis without violating optical element order.
The 30-page Chinese SimSun PDF passed automated PDF QA and manual visual inspection.
